name: IL-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district with incumbent Darin LaHood holding a roughly $6.3M-to-$289K cash advantage
Prediction markets price LaHood's reelection near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; the race rests on fundamentals
A Democratic-tilted national environment is the main source of uncertainty
model.rationale: LaHood combines an R+11 district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money edge, while markets price his reelection around 96 percent; only the nationally favorable climate for Democrats points the other way, and it is unlikely to close a gap of this size.
model.watch: A strong Democratic wave or surprise polling showing Paul Nolley within single digits would be the clearest sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 16th District leans Republican by about eleven points, and incumbent Darin LaHood is seeking another term with a commanding financial edge: roughly $6.3 million on hand compared with about $289,000 for Democrat Paul Nolley. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets price LaHood's chances at about 96 percent.

The main source of uncertainty is the national environment, which currently favors Democrats and could narrow margins in a wave year. Still, the combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising advantage makes an upset unlikely. The forecast expects LaHood to win by a double-digit margin, with Nolley needing a dramatic shift in the political climate to make this race genuinely competitive.
